paper_sections.title: Differential patterns of cortical activation as a function of fluid reasoning complexity.
fMRI Subject Selection and Behavioral Task
Functional Differences Between High-gfand Low-gf Samples

description.value: The study investigated how fluid reasoning complexity modulates cortical activity differently in participants with high and low fluid intelligence, using fMRI during moderate and complex Raven-type reasoning tasks.

design.value: Two groups selected from the extreme tails of fluid-intelligence scores performed moderate figural, complex analytic, and control matrix tasks during two fMRI runs; functional activity was analyzed within and between groups using whole-group and group-specific random-effects analyses and ROI-based repeated-measures ANOVA.

task_description.value: A computerized behavioral task composed by a total of 32 fluid reasoning and 32 control problems adapted from both the RSPM and RAPM.

presentation_software.value: E-Prime software, v.1.1, Psychology Software Tools

instructions.value: The subject was instructed to take all the time necessary for generating the solution and when ready to press the button beneath his/her left index finger; subjects were explicitly taught not to guess the solution.

stimuli.value: 3 × 3 Raven matrices with a missing bottom-right entry and eight alternatives; figural, analytic, and control problems.

task_performance_measures.value: reasoning times; number of correct responses; error rates; percentages of missing responses; reaction times in the match period

description.value: BOLD contrast functional images were acquired with T2*-weighted echo planar imaging (EPI) free induction decay sequences; 16 transaxial slices, two runs for each functional session.

pulse_sequence_type.value: T2*-weighted echo planar imaging (EPI) free induction decay sequences

description.value: A high resolution structural volume was acquired at the end of the session via a 3D MPRAGE sequence.

model_settings.value: Predictors of interest were correct analytic, error analytic, correct figural, and error figural conditions. The control task was baseline; instruction and match conditions were predictors of no interest. The boxcar waveform representing rest and task conditions was convolved with the hemodynamic response function. Temporal autocorrelation was corrected.

estimator.value: GLM parameters (beta values) estimated in individual subject analysis

model_settings.value: Individual-subject GLM beta values were entered in a second-level voxel-wise random effect analysis. Group activation maps contrasted predictors of interest with the control task and were thresholded at P < 0.05 corrected for multiple comparisons by the Bonferroni method.
A 6 × 2 × 2 × 2 analysis of variance with factors ROI, hemisphere, condition, and groups; Bonferroni correction for multiple comparisons.

description.value: Problems requiring a single perceptually based rule, such as Constant in a Row or Quantitative Pair-wise Progression.
Problems requiring abstraction of more than a rule or of a single rule based on analytic reasoning.
3 × 3 matrices with all entries containing figural elements devoid of any logical relations; participants were asked to look across rows and down columns and then at the eight pseudo-alternatives.
The instruction “solve” preceded reasoning matrices and “watch” preceded control matrices; each instruction lasted 1,200 ms.
A maximum 1,500-ms period in which a red cross overlapped one of eight alternatives and the participant matched the generated response with the computer suggestion.
Analytic reasoning problems for which a correct response was given.
Analytic reasoning problems for which an incorrect response was given.
Figural reasoning problems for which a correct response was given.
Figural reasoning problems for which an incorrect response was given.
